lines.text:
I've heard this novel described as a 'fever dream' and frankly that is probably the most accurate way to describe it. Like most of Faulkner's works, I wouldn't say this novel is easy to read - which is why most folks give up 20 pages in. But I think those who have read anything by Faulkner would agree that his works become more and more rewarding as the plot continues to unfold. Just brew that pot of coffee and settle in for a slow burn.

Side Note: I'm continually amazed by the way Faulkner can turn a mundane conversation or description into something incredibly eloquent.

lines.text:
I’ve struggled for years to find the words to review this book. I still remember picking up a copy in a Fargo, ND bookstore whilst interning for John Deere. Read it in a single weekend.

This Side of Paradise is smart. It’s poetic. Eloquent in the way only Fitzgerald can be.

And it’s still, to date, the best book I’ve ever read.

Armory Blaine is eternal - as well as F Scott.
